title: MorphADMET Links Chemical Structure and Cellular Morphology for Context Dependent ADMET Assessment
content: Cellular morphology captures compound-induced changes in cell state, but the relationship between the magnitude of these changes and absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties remains dependent on the endpoint and assay context. We developed MorphADMET to examine these relationships and evaluate complementary prediction and reference-retrieval tasks across six imaging datasets, seven morphological representations, eleven binary endpoints, and aqueous solubility. Endpoint comparisons used differences in median morphological response with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals from 2,000 resamples. Positive compounds showed greater responses in selected contexts, including A549–Ames, HUVEC–CYP1A2, HUVEC–CYP3A4, and HRCE–CYP2D6, whereas U2OS hERG-negative compounds showed greater responses. Structure-based ensembles predicted strong morphological responses with average precision (AP) of 0.353–0.472 and outperformed a compact descriptor baseline in four of five contexts. Models using measured morphology showed endpoint-dependent discrimination, including AP of 0.601 and AUROC of 0.786 for hERG in A549 cells. Exploratory compartment-level analyses identified differences in nuclear texture, cytoplasmic organization, and cell shape between endpoint-label groups. In the structure-based ADMET benchmark, MorphADMET achieved the highest observed AP for four of eleven classification endpoints and the lowest solubility mean absolute error, 0.660 log10 mol/L. Morphology-selected reference compounds showed higher class-balanced hERG label agreement than random references in all six cellular contexts. A CYP2D6 neighborhood illustrated shared physicochemical properties alongside partial scaffold similarity. These findings support endpoint-specific use of chemical and morphological information for compound assessment, while distinguishing overall perturbation, predictive discrimination, and retrospective reference agreement.
